job.title: 106. Integrity Industrial - Parks and Gardens Co-Ordinator
job.description:
Integrity Industrial is currently seeking an experienced Parks & Horticulture Coordinator to support the Operations Manager at a Government Facility in Burswood. This is a hands-on, field-based role responsible for overseeing horticultural, turf and landscape maintenance activities across one of Perth's premier parklands.

This position would suit a highly experienced horticultural professional with strong technical knowledge of turf management, irrigation systems, contractor management, and landscape maintenance.

Key Responsibilities
  • Oversee the delivery of horticultural, turf and landscape maintenance services across Burswood Park.
  • Monitor and manage the performance of grounds maintenance contractors to ensure services meet operational and contractual standards.
  • Provide specialist advice on horticulture, turf management, arboriculture, irrigation and landscape maintenance.
  • Coordinate turf and landscape reinstatement works following major events.
  • Monitor the condition of horticultural assets and implement corrective actions as required.
  • Support the planning, delivery and continuous improvement of grounds maintenance programs.
  • Contribute to horticultural planning, reporting and resource management.
  • Promote safe work practices and ensure compliance with relevant WHS legislation and procedures.

Essential Skills & Experience
  • Proven hands-on experience in a field-based horticulture, turf management or parks maintenance role.
  • Experience restoring and managing broadacre turf in golf courses, sports fields or similar environments.
  • Strong technical knowledge of herbicides, fertilisers and plant growth regulators.
  • Experience managing large-scale irrigation systems, ideally Toro Lynx.
  • Sound knowledge of turf and grounds maintenance equipment and operational practices.
  • Strong understanding of workplace health and safety requirements relating to chemicals, plant and contractor management.
  • Ability to work independently with minimal technical supervision.

Requirements
  • Current WA Driver's Licence (mandatory)
  • White Card (preferred)
  • Certificate III in Horticulture (desirable)
  • Turf, arboriculture, horticulture or related qualifications highly regarded
  • National Police Clearance (within 6 months or willing to obtain)

Assignment Details
  • 37.5 hours per week
  • Flexibility required between 6:30am and 5:30pm to meet operational and event requirements
  • 5-month casualassignment
  • Immediate start available

What's on Offer?
  • Opportunity to work within one of Perth's most iconic parklands
  • Diverse role combining horticulture, turf management, irrigation and contractor coordination
  • Autonomy and variety in a technically focused environment
  • Supportive team and dynamic outdoor workplace

If you have a strong background in horticulture, parks maintenance or turf management and are looking for your next challenge, we'd love to hear from you. Apply now with your current resume.

job.title: 99. Integrity Industrial - Camera Operator
job.description:
We are currently seeking Camera Operators for multiple opportunities across Western Australia.

This is a hands-on, operational role responsible for the deployment and operation of mobile traffic camera equipment, contributing to road safety across WA. You’ll work independently across allocated locations, setting up and monitoring camera equipment, completing operational records and ensuring equipment is operated safely and accurately.

The assignment will run until 30/06/2027

Current vacancies
  • Neerabup
  • Mandurah
  • Geraldton
  • Midland

The role
As a Camera Operator, your duties will include:
  • Travelling to allocated camera locations and setting up, repositioning and operating mobile camera equipment
  • Monitoring and checking camera equipment to ensure it is operating accurately
  • Undertaking preliminary fault diagnosis and reporting equipment issues
  • Recording operational and location information and maintaining accurate documentation
  • Ensuring camera equipment, vehicles and associated equipment remain safe and secure
  • Communicating professionally with members of the public when required
  • Driving independently to camera sites across metropolitan and/or regional locations
  • Preparing operational reports and documentation, including information that may be required for court proceedings.


Hours & roster
These positions are 75 hours per fortnight, working a rotating three-week roster.
The standard rotation consists of:
  • 8 afternoon shifts
  • 2 days off
  • 7 day shifts
  • 4 days off

Standard shifts are 7.5 hours

Typical shift times include:
  • Day shift: 7:00am – 2:30pm
  • Afternoon shift: 2:30pm – 10:00pm
  • School zone day shift: 6:00am – 1:30pm
  • School zone afternoon shift: 1:00pm – 8:30pm


There are also opportunities for voluntary overtime in addition to standard rostered hours. This may be approximately 3 additional hours per day, up to a maximum of 5 days per swing.

About you
To be considered, you will need:
  • A current Western Australian C or CA Class Driver’s Licence
  • The physical capacity to lift and move bulky camera equipment
  • Good communication skills and the confidence to interact with members of the public, including managing difficult situations professionally
  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to undertake basic equipment fault diagnosis
  • Good attention to detail and the ability to maintain accurate operational records
  • The ability to work independently and safely across different locations
  • Flexibility to work a rotating roster
  • National Police Clearance
  • Australian Citizen or Permanent Resident

Training
Successful candidates will undertake two weeks of training in Midland before commencing in the position.
